record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let A be a zero sequence for L^2_a(D), let phi_A be the zero divisor associated with A, and let I(A) be the invariant subspace of functions in L^2_a(D) that vanish on A. Does phi_A generate I(A) as an invariant subspace, equivalently do phi_A, z phi_A, z^2 phi_A, and so on span a dense subspace of I(A)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty,$$
where $dA$ is the normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. A sequence $A=\{a_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities) is called a zero sequence for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ if there exists a nonzero $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ whose zero set (counted with multiplicity) contains $A$. Define
$$I(A)=\{f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D}):f\text{ vanishes on }A\text{ (with multiplicity)}\},$$
which is a closed subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ invariant under multiplication by $z$. Let $\varphi_A\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the extremal (canonical) zero divisor associated with $A$, namely the unique solution of the extremal problem
$$\sup\{\operatorname{Re} f(0_A):f\in I(A),\ \|f\|=1\},$$
where $0_A$ is the lowest-order nontrivial Taylor coefficient functional determined by $A$ (so that $\varphi_A$ has unit norm in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ and vanishes on $A$).

Question: Does $\varphi_A$ generate $I(A)$ as an invariant subspace under multiplication by $z$? Equivalently, is the linear span of $\{\varphi_A,\,z\varphi_A,\,z^2\varphi_A,\dots\}$ dense in $I(A)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively by Aleman, Richter, and Sundberg in "Beurling's theorem for the Bergman space" (Acta Mathematica 177 (1996), 275–310). Their theorem implies in particular that for any zero-based invariant subspace $I(A)$, the extremal zero divisor $\varphi_A$ generates $I(A)$ under multiplication by $z$.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's theorem for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Aleman, Richter and Sundberg showed that if M is an invariant subspace of the Bergman space A²(D), then M = [M ⊖ zM]
status_evidence.claim: Aleman-Richter-Sundberg's Beurling-type theorem implies that the extremal zero divisor generates the zero-based invariant subspace.

status_evidence.title: Contractive Zero-Divisors in Bergman Spaces (Duren, Khavinson, Shapiro, Sundberg)
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier work introducing the contractive zero-divisor phi_A in Bergman spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The extremal/contractive zero divisor phi_A is the standard object whose generation property is in question.
